Results and verificationMethods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Solve dimensionless −uₓₓ=π² sin(πx) on [0,1] with zero Dirichlet data. Use sixteen hidden units, 49 real parameters, seeds 8401–8403, 64 training points and 257 separate evaluation points. Editorial clarification This fixed-budget study covers one smooth Poisson problem and three seeds. A small training loss does not establish independent-point accuracy or general PINN training success. Unmet goals remain visible. Adopted numerical method Train a hard-boundary tanh ansatz with trust-region reflective least squares and an analytic parameter Jacobian. Retain every returned model under the fixed budget. Also solve second-order finite differences with 31, 63 and 127 unknowns using the Thomas algorithm. −uxx=π2sin⁡(πx),0<x<1,u(0)=u(1)=0−uxx​=π2sin(πx),0<x<1,u(0)=u(1)=0 uθ(x)=x(1−x)[b0+∑j=116ajtanh⁡(wjx+bj)]uθ​(x)=x(1−x)[b0​+j=1∑16​aj​tanh(wj​x+bj​)] ri=−uθ,xx(xi)−π2sin⁡(πxi)π2,L=164∑i=164ri2ri​=π2−uθ,xx​(xi​)−π2sin(πxi​)​,L=641​i=1∑64​ri2​ References and measured quantities Independently qualify all 49 residual-Jacobian columns, loss-gradient coordinates and spatial derivatives.
